entries.content:
Done. The root cause was a set of deliberate corruptions in `glom/matching.py`:

1. **`_precedence`** — its return values were scrambled (empty tuple/frozenset returned 1 instead of 0, `max` was changed to `min`, types returned 3, glomit-specs 2, and constants −1). Restored to: constants → 0, types → 1, glomit-bearing specs → 2, composite tuple/frozenset keys → `max` of item precedences (0 if empty). This fixes `Optional()`/`Required()` validation (`ValueError: Optional() keys must...`) and dict-key ordering.
2. **`_Bool._m_repr` and `Not._m_repr`** — the polarity of the checks was inverted (wrong child inspected, `not` applied to recursion), breaking operator-style reprs like `(M == 1) & float` and `~(M)`. Restored so M-style repr is used only when the first child (or `Not`'s child) is an `_MType`/`_MExpr` or a nested boolean combinator that itself uses M-style repr.
3. **`_handle_dict`** — several saboteurs: spec keys were no longer sorted by `_precedence`; the required-keys check used precedence `== 1` instead of `== 0` (constants are required by default); the defaults comprehension used `or key.default is _MISSING` instead of `and key.default is not _MISSING` (causing `AttributeError` on plain keys); results were stored under `result[val]` instead of `result[key]` (broken key mappings); `Required(...)` keys weren't unwrapped before matching; a target key matching no spec key silently passed instead of raising `MatchError("key {0} didn't match any of {1}")`; and the missing-keys message had a stray colon.

All 200 existing tests pass, module doctests (which encode the exact error messages) pass, and the issue's reproduction cases plus extra edge cases (precedence ordering, Optional/Required defaults, composite keys, repr round-tripping) all verify correctly.
